tool.name: spaCy NER from Hugging Face
tool.description: find named entities with one or more spaCy pipelines from Hugging Face

tool.help:
**spaCy NER from Hugging Face** runs a named-entity pipeline from the Hugging Face Hub over your text, so you can use your own trained models without installing them on the server. Input ----- * **Plain text**: paragraphs separated by blank lines (the lines of a paragraph are joined), or one paragraph per line. * **TEI/XML**: the text of every ``

`` element is one paragraph. * **JSON / JSON Lines**: objects with a ``text`` field (a list, or one per line). Other fields, and spans that are already there, are kept. Output ------ One file in JSON Lines format (one JSON object per line, one line per paragraph):: {"text": "The Cyclades ...", "spans": [{"start": 4, "end": 12, "label": "PLACE"}]} ``start`` and ``end`` are character positions in ``text``. Galaxy has no JSON Lines datatype, so the file is labelled ``json``. Add several **NER models** to run them over the same text, for example place, method, activity and goal. All models are loaded first, so a wrong name or an incompatible model stops the job at once. Then the first model runs over the whole text, then the second, and so on. Every entity goes into the same ``spans`` list with the label of its model (or the label you set). Entities of different models can overlap. Models ------ Give the repository as ``owner/name``. It must be a spaCy pipeline with ``meta.json`` and ``config.cfg`` at its root and a ``ner`` component, as made by ``spacy huggingface-hub push``. The model is downloaded when the job runs, so the server needs internet access and the first run takes a while for large models. Pipelines are code and weights from the Hub. Only use models you trust. Models saved with ``spacy-transformers`` 2.x need a newer environment than this version of the tool provides. If that is the case, the job stops and says which version the model asks for.
